key_insight: LiveSense converts a COTS laptop Wi‑Fi NIC (Intel AX211/BE201) into a real‑time, centimeter‑level Range–Doppler sensor while keeping normal network communication active.
problem_solved: Enables high-resolution RF sensing from commodity laptops without disabling or modifying the Wi‑Fi link, overcoming synchronization, self‑interference and timing alignment challenges that previously required specialized hardware.
method: High-rate (>= 40 Hz) extraction of fully synchronized Channel State Information (CSI) from Intel AX211 / BE201 NICs on a cross‑platform laptop implementation.
On‑device time and phase alignment plus self‑interference cancellation to separate sensing signals from ongoing communication traffic in real time.
Real‑time Range–Doppler processing pipeline that outputs centimeter‑scale range and velocity maps while preserving simultaneous Wi‑Fi communication.
impact: Provides a low‑cost, software‑only sensing platform for Edge AI — enabling real‑time dataset collection, gesture/activity recognition, and embedded ML inference directly on commodity laptops without extra hardware.
visual_elements: Schematic laptop diagram showing NIC antenna, concurrent Wi‑Fi data flow and sensing pipeline (CSI → alignment → cancellation → RD map).
Sample Range–Doppler heatmap illustrating centimeter resolution and velocity peaks for a moving target.
Pipeline flowchart with latency/Hz annotations (CSI capture ≥40 Hz, on‑device processing steps).
Comparison bar chart of cost/complexity vs. specialized radar hardware highlighting COTS advantage.
paper_title: LiveSense: A Real-Time Wi-Fi Sensing Platform for Range-Doppler on COTS Laptop
paper_authors: Jessica Sanson, Rahul C. Shah, Maximilian Pinaroc, Cagri Tanriover, Valerio Frascolla
